To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed and implemented a new DVS that is 10× more sensitive than the state of the art, has a 4× smaller power consumption, 2× lower FPN, and 2× smaller area per pixel.

(i) the proposed pixel photo sensing stage, which includes a 3-stage transimpedance amplifier (TIA), a comparator and a 1-bit digital counter, achieves 1.5%, 3 μs latency, 0.9%, 4 mW, 120 dB DR, 3 decades intrascene DR, and 30 × 30 μm2 per pixel; (ii) the proposed TIA achieves 1.7% contrast sensitivity,

A novel pixel photo sensing stage and transimpedances preamplification stage have been designed, which allow to improve contrast sensitivity (down 1.5%), power (down 4 mW) and reduce fixed pattern noise (down 0.9%) while maintaining the lowest reported latency (3 µs) and good dynamic range (120 dB).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of vision sensors that have the potential for a wide range of applications.
the design of low-power CMOS image sensors with high-speed, low latency, and high dynamic range for real-time vision applications.
the development of a novel CMOS DVS pixel, and the design and fabrication of a 128 × 124 DVS test prototype.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new DVS architecture presented here is the best performing one reported so far in terms of all the key DVS parameters.
the DVS is now a mature and reliable technology, with a very good performance and a large potential in many application fields.

the DVS has now reached the maturity level to be seriously considered for a wide range of real-world applications, and the results reported in this paper make it possible to consider the DVS as a serious contender for a wide range applications in the fields mentioned above.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved the best contrast sensitivity, lowest power, and lowest FPN, and the shortest latency among DVSs reported in literature, while maintaining good Dynamic Range.
the proposed pixel design has the best performance reported for DVS pixels in terms of contrast sensitivity, fixed pattern noise, latency, and power.
a DVS with 1.5 × 1.5 mm 2 active area, 3.5 mW power, 1.5 % contrast sensitivity, 0.9 % FPN, 3 μs latency, 120 dB dynamic range and 30 × 30 μm 2 area per pixel is reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
contrast coding is not limited by the pixel itself but by the transimpedance amplifier stage.
the contrast sensitivity of DVS can be significantly improved without compromising other key features.
the DVS architecture is a viable option for a new generation of low power, high-speed vision systems.
